 Live Last Update October 29, 2026, 8:57 PM EDT US military preparing options for Trump after he says 'anything's possible' with Iran, officials say
 Official and military sources told Fox News that movements are being made in the Middle East to give President Donald Trump options if he decides to resume attacks against Iran. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu reportedly is pushing for fresh strikes on the Iranian regime.
 Share on Facebook 
 Share on Twitter 
 Share on Flipboard 
 Share by Email 
 Your Preview Pass expires in 00:00 Sign In with TV Provider Don't have a TV subscription? Sign Up WHAT TO KNOW
 The U.S. Embassy in Riyadh warned Wednesday of potential attacks on airports and travel disruptions in Saudi Arabia, citing missile and drone attacks by Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen.
 Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said his country and the U.S. have a chance to remove the Iranian threat "once and for all."
 Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan spoke with President Donald Trump on Wednesday and offered Ankara's support for efforts to end the war in Ukraine while highlighting ongoing security concerns in the Middle East.
 Trump said Iran's military is struggling to produce drones during Operation Epic Fury because it no longer has access to electricity, hampering its weapons production.
 An Israeli soldier was charged with passing military information to Iranian intelligence agents in exchange for cryptocurrency.
 Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis urged European Union member states to increase their naval deployments in the Red Sea, warning that Houthi strikes continue to jeopardize shipping.
 A tanker was struck by an unknown projectile while exiting the Strait of Hormuz , according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO).
 Saudi air defense forces shot down two missiles fired toward Riyadh by the Houthis, a coalition spokesman said.
 Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf rejected Washington’s diplomatic strategy and drew a firm line on negotiations, saying any agreement to end the war would need acceptance of Tehran’s seven conditions.
 25 Posts Sort by Newest Oldest incoming update… 1 hour ago Pinned Fired Pentagon general admits leaking classified Iran, Ukraine intel: report 
 Army Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia / U.S. Army photo by Staff Sgt. Kaden D. Pitt Army Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia, a former senior Pentagon strategist, admitted to leaking classified information about U.S. policies toward Iran and Ukraine to two reporters, Axios reported Thursday.
 An internal Pentagon investigation is said to have found that Sylvia admitted to the leaks on video after failing four polygraph tests. War Secretary Pete Hegseth later fired the three-star general.
 Sylvia, who served in the Joint Chiefs of Staff's Directorate for Strategy, Plans and Policy, made “unauthorized disclosures to the media,” investigators concluded.
 The leaks began as early as June 2025 and involved encrypted Signal messages and a meeting with a reporter at an Arlington, Virginia, diner, according to Axios.
 Investigators said Sylvia also used handwritten notes from a classified document to disclose details of U.S. military aid to Ukraine.
 Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said Thursday the case had been referred to the Justice Department for possible prosecution.
 “Classified information is not personal property,” Parnell wrote on X. 
 “Leaking it for personal, political or professional gain is a betrayal of the trust placed in those responsible for keeping it.”
 “Our commitment was not an empty promise,” he added. “We vowed to find you, and we meant it.”
 Posted by Emma Bussey Share 19 mins ago Yemeni military urges investigation into alleged Houthi chemical shelling in Taiz 
 Yemen’s armed forces said Thursday they were treating reports that Houthi militants had fired shells containing suspected toxic substances in Taiz with the utmost seriousness.
 The alleged attack reportedly caused civilians and Popular Resistance fighters to experience suffocation and fainting.
 "The Armed Forces are taking reports seriously regarding the use of poisonous gases by the terrorist Houthi militia in Taiz," the official military spokesperson said, calling for an investigation.
 Posted by Emma Bussey Share 34 mins ago US envoy Waltz warns Iran over nuclear program as UN watchdog demands inspections 
 U.S. Ambassador to the UN Michael Waltz warned against Iran’s nuclear ambitions Thursday amid mounting concerns over Tehran’s refusal to allow monitoring at its nuclear sites.
 “The Iranian regime can point fingers all it wants, but it cannot explain away its failure to cooperate with the UN’s IAEA for inspections,” Waltz said.
 “The world needs to hear this loud and clear: The United States and our partners will NEVER allow Iran to obtain a nuclear weapon. Period. End of story,” he added on X .
 His remarks came after the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) said this week that inspectors must be allowed back onto Tehran's sites to verify its program.
 Posted by Emma Bussey Share 36 mins ago Yemeni forces launch hundreds of strikes on Houthis, claim 324 fighters killed in 24 hours 
 The Yemeni Armed Forces intensified their major military offensive under Operation "Dawn of Yemen" on Thursday, carrying out hundreds of precision strikes over the previous 24 hours.
 "These operations struck reinforcements of the terrorist Houthi militia, their advanced command and control centers, their field commanders, their sniper positions, their sources of fire, and their supply means," Al-Nuzaili said on X.
 Al-Nuzaili said the operations neutralized 324 militia commanders and fighters and destroyed or disabled 108 vehicles and military equipment.
 Posted by Emma Bussey Share 2 hours ago Shrapnel from intercepted Houthi missile injures Saudi citizen: report 
 A Saudi citizen was wounded in Riyadh on Thursday by falling shrapnel after air defenses shot down two ballistic missiles launched by Houthi forces, according to Saudi Civil Defense authorities.
 A spokesperson told the state-run news agency that the debris also caused damage to a home and a vehicle. 
 The Saudi-led coalition had earlier announced on X that it successfully intercepted and destroyed both incoming missiles targeting the capital.
 Posted by Emma Bussey Share 2 hours ago Sen. Murphy warns renewed US strikes on Iran could trigger 'devastating escalation' 
 Sen. Chris Murphy, warned Thursday that a potential U.S. military plan to resume operations against Iran could trigger a devastating escalation of the conflict and threaten American national security interests.
 "In one of these briefings we did get the chance to have a fairly detailed conversation about what the war plan would be if we restarted military operations," Murphy said during an event at the Middle East Institute .
 "You've heard a preview that it would be a short duration plan," he said. "I will just say this: Their plan is insane."
 Murphy also warned that the plan could lead to "devastating escalation and the likely destruction of our commitment to the rule of law."
 "I mean, there's been open reporting as to, you know, what we may be planning and the civilian infrastructure that we may be targeting," Murphy said.
 "I think the plan, the plan that they have, they have certainly been asked by the president to develop a plan," he continued.
 "Whether they believe it will work or not, I do not know, but the plan that they have developed will lead, in my view, to a prolongment and an escalation of this war that will be devastating for our security interests," Murphy said.
 Posted by Emma Bussey Share 3 hours ago Greek PM urges EU to deploy more warships to Red Sea amid Houthi attacks 
 Houthis / Red Sea / Al Joumhouriya TV / Handout via Reuters Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis urged European Union member states on Thursday to increase their naval deployments in the Red Sea , warning that Houthi strikes continue to jeopardize shipping.
 "My argument is simple: the European Union has an interest in having a concrete presence with hard assets in this part of the world, and we need more countries to participate in Aspides," he told Reuters .
 The EU established Operation Aspides in 2024 to safeguard merchant vessels traveling through the key shipping corridor.
 Greece, Italy and France have also supplied warships to the mission, but Mitsotakis stressed that resources are "clearly not enough."
 Posted by Emma Bussey Share 4 hours ago Israeli soldier charged with spying for Iran, leaking military secrets in exchange for crypto 
 Israeli military / Amir Levy / Getty Images An Israeli soldier was charged with passing military information to Iranian intelligence agents in exchange for cryptocurrency, Iran International reported Thursday citing Israeli security officials.
 The soldier, who was arrested in September after an investigation maintained contact with Iranian operatives for roughly a year.
 Authorities said the soldier provided information on military bases, troop readiness, and call-ups, including details of his own mobilization at the outbreak of the war with Iran in February.
 Prosecutors alleged he photographed missile interceptors, military vehicles, and U.S. refueling aircraft at an Israeli airport, while also sharing details about fellow soldiers and commanders despite knowing Iranian handlers could target them for recruitment.
 The soldier was also allegedly offered $200,000 to travel to Iran and instructed to install encrypted messaging apps.
 Military prosecutors formally charged him with contacting a foreign agent and passing information to the enemy with the intent to harm national security, the outlet said.
 Posted by Emma Bussey Share 5 hours ago ExxonMobil, Chevron execs pull out of major Mideast oil summit over security fears: report 
 Oil Tanker / REUTERS / Benoit Tessier U.S. energy giants ExxonMobil and Chevron pulled their top executives from next week's flagship ADIPEC conference in Abu Dhabi, citing security concerns, Reuters reported Thursday.
 Exxon Chief Executive Darren Woods and Chevron Upstream President Clay Neff were both set to attend the Middle East's premier oil and gas summit before the cancellations, the outlet said.
 The State Department also last week ordered some diplomats to leave Saudi Arabia, which has been facing nearby Houthi strikes.
 Posted by Emma Bussey Share 6 hours ago Tanker hit by projectile while leaving Strait of Hormuz, UK maritime authority says 
 A tanker was struck by an unknown projectile while exiting the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO).
 “A Company Security Officer has informed UKMTO that their tanker has been struck by an unknown projectile whilst completing an outbound transit of the Strait of Hormuz ,” UKMTO said in a statement.
 The maritime authority also said there were no reported injuries to the crew or reports of environmental damage.
 “Vessels are advised to transit with caution and report any suspicious activity to UKMTO, whilst authorities investigate,” UKMTO added.
 Posted by Emma Bussey Share 6 hours ago Saudi Arabia shoots down 2 Houthi missiles aimed at Riyadh amid warnings across kingdom 
 Saudi air defense forces shot down two missiles fired toward Riyadh on Thursday by the Houthis, a coalition spokesman said.
 “Air defenses intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by the terrorist Houthi militia towards Riyadh,” Col. Turki al-Malki, a spokesman for the Saudi-led coalition, said in a post on X .
 Earlier, civil defense authorities issued alerts warning of potential danger in Riyadh, Al Kharj and Najran, according to Reuters .
 Posted by Emma Bussey Share 6 hours ago Iran draws hard line on ending war, demands US accept 7 conditions before deal 
 Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf on Thursday rejected Washington’s diplomatic strategy and drew a firm line on negotiations, saying any agreement to end the war would need acceptance of Tehran’s seven conditions.
 “Iran’s conditions have been repeatedly and clearly stated to the mediators,” Ghalibaf said on X.
 “The carrot-and-stick approach has no effect on Iran. Progress can only be achieved once Iran’s seven conditions have been agreed upon,” he added.
 Posted by Emma Bussey Share 7 hours ago Sen. Murphy says it would be 'insane' to restart war against Iran after midterm elections 
 Sen. Chris Murphy, D-Conn., speaks during a Senate Appropriations Committee hearing on President Donald Trump's supplemental funding request for the Department of War, in Washington, D.C., on July 21, 2026. (Eric Lee/Reuters) Sen. Chris Murphy, D-Conn., said Thursday that it would be "insane" for the Trump administration to resume the war against Iran after Election Day. 
 "Trump is reportedly planning to restart war with Iran after the election," Murphy wrote on X. "Some of us have been briefed on the war plan. And while I cannot disclose any details, I can say this: the plan is insane. It will not achieve objectives and will set off a new cycle of escalation." 
 Murphy shared a clip of him speaking Wednesday at The Middle East Institute in Washington, D.C., where he said a resumption of U.S. military action against Iran "would lead to devastating escalation and the likely destruction to our commitment to the rule of law."
 Posted by Greg Norman-Diamond Share 8 hours ago Ship seen 'on fire' in Strait of Hormuz was involved in 'maritime security incident,' UKMTO says 
 Cargo ships lie at anchor in the Strait of Hormuz off Bandar Abbas, Iran, on Oct. 24, 2026. (Amirhosein Khorgooi/ISNA via AP) The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations Centre (UKMTO) said Thursday that a ship previously spotted "on fire" in the Strait of Hormuz has sunk. 
 The incident was reported about nine nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman.  
 "Regional authorities have identified the vessel as a dhow, which was involved in a maritime security incident, igniting a large fire onboard causing the dhow to list and sink," the UKMTO said in a post on X. 
 "Local authorities have confirmed that the crew have been safely evacuated," it added. 
 Posted by Greg Norman-Diamond Share 8 hours ago Iran has created secret network to get military hardware, explosives past US barriers: report 
 A projectile reaches an imported Iveco truck at a location given as Iran during what U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) says are strikes targeting Iranian mobile missile-launch capabilities, in this screengrab taken from a handout video released on March 5, 2026. (CENTCOM/Reuters) The Iranian regime has used a vast financial and military network to import at least $2 billion in hardware, explosives and trucks around the U.S. naval blockade and sanctions since the beginning of last year, according to a Reuters investigation. 
 The news agency reported Thursday that more than 5,000 agencies form the network, which has helped Tehran acquire weapons components involved in the creation of missiles and drones, and heavy-duty trucks that can serve as missile launchers, among other materials. 
 Reuters said it based its investigation on Iranian bank and government records, corporate filings and import data. Some of the agencies, it added, are linked to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and they operate through frontmen and foreign shell companies, who purchase items for Iran using profits from illicit oil sales. 
 The material flows into Iran by cargo ship across the Caspian Sea from Russia, by trucks from Central Asia and planes from China, Reuters also reported. 
 A Treasury Department spokeswoman told Reuters that the U.S. “has severed the regime’s economic lifelines.” 
 “While the regime may continue its desperate attempts to evade our powerful sanctions, fund its military and weapons programs, and access foreign currency, we are always 10 steps ahead,” she reportedly added. 
 Posted by Greg Norman-Diamond Share 9 hours ago Trump says fired Pentagon strategist is going to have 'big problems' 
 President Donald Trump speaks to reporters before boarding Air Force One for travel to South Carolina, at Joint Base Andrews, Md., on Oct. 29, 2026. (Jonathan Ernst/Reuters) President Donald Trump suggested Thursday that Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia, one of the Pentagon’s senior strategic planners who was fired by Secretary of War Pete Hegseth over allegations of leaking classified information to journalists, is going to have "big problems."
 Trump told reporters ahead of his departure to a midterms rally in South Carolina that his administration is "very much looking for leakers." 
 A Department of War official told Fox News that Sylvia leaked classified information to journalists about the Iran war, Russia’s war in Ukraine and other sensitive matters.
 The official added that Sylvia failed three polygraph examinations related to alleged disclosures of classified information. The investigation has been referred to the Justice Department. 
 Fox News' Jennifer Griffin and Morgan Phillips contributed to this post. 
 Posted by Greg Norman-Diamond Share 10 hours ago UK is 'doing everything we can' to reopen Strait of Hormuz, Burnham says 
 British Prime Minister Andy Burnham. (Reuters/Jack Taylor) British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Thursday that the United Kingdom is "doing everything we can" to get the Strait of Hormuz opened during the U.S.-Iran War.  
 "We are doing everything that we can to de-escalate the situation, to support the full reopening of the Strait of Hormuz," Burnham said, noting that he raised the issue with President Donald Trump last week, according to Reuters. 
 "But, of course, it's without any nuclear capability in Iran," Burnham reportedly added. 
 The remarks come as U.S. Central Command is enforcing a blockade of Iranian ports in the region. 
 "More than 3,000 commercial vessels have successfully transited the Strait of Hormuz with support from CENTCOM forces over the last six months," CENTCOM said earlier this week. 
 Posted by Greg Norman-Diamond Share 11 hours ago CENTCOM rejects Iran's claim that it captured a US drone near Strait of Hormuz 
 U.S. Central Command pushed back Thursday after Iran claimed it captured an American surveillance drone near the Strait of Hormuz.
 Iranian state television reported Thursday that Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), in an “electronic warfare operation,” detected and identified the MQM-170 Outlaw drone, and took control of its control systems before landing it in Iranian territory, according to The Associated Press.
 It did not say when the drone was allegedly seized.
 “In the past weeks and months, the IRGC has repeatedly lied out of desperation, and today is no different,” U.S. Navy Capt. Tim Hawkins, CENTCOM's spokesperson, told the AP.
 The Associated Press contributed to this post. 
 Posted by Greg Norman-Diamond Share 11 hours ago Ship seen 'on fire' in the Strait of Hormuz, UKMTO says 
 The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations Centre (UKMTO) said Thursday that a ship was spotted "on fire" in the Strait of Hormuz.  
 The incident was reported about nine nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman. 
 "The Master of a third-party vessel has reported sighting another vessel on fire," the UKMTO said. 
 "Status of crew is unknown," it added. "There is no damage assessment or environmental impact report at present." 
 Posted by Greg Norman-Diamond Share 12 hours ago Hegseth fired top military planner over severe misconduct, alleged leaks, official says 
 Maj. Gen. Brett Sylvia, at a 101st Airborne Division change of command ceremony at Fort Campbell, Ky., May 30, 2025. (Sgt. Timothy Jackson/U.S Army via AP) Secretary of War Pete Hegseth fired Army Lt. Gen Brett Sylvia, a key war planner in the Pentagon, alleging that Sylvia met with journalists to leak classified information, the Department of War said.
 A Department of War official said Sylvia, despite having the title of Directorate for Strategy, Plans, and Policy at the Joint Chiefs of Staff, otherwise known in the military as the J5, was not a central planner for Operation Epic Fury against Iran, a campaign that is under the responsibility of U.S. Central Command and its leader, Navy Adm. Brad Cooper. 
 Sylvia is being investigated for leaking classified information about the Iran war, the Russia-Ukraine conflict and more, the official told Fox News.  
 The official alleged Sylvia started meeting with journalists outside the Pentagon to leak classified information because of a Pentagon media policy mandating that journalists have escorts while inside the building. 
 The official also said the investigation into Sylvia remains active and has been referred to the Department of Justice, noting Hegseth took immediate action and fire Sylvia in order to protect national security. 
 The Atlantic first reported the firing and said Sylvia did not respond to a request for comment.
 Fox News' Jennifer Griffin contributed to this post.
